title: Priority allocation for top accounts through cycle lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a deterministic, capacity-aware lane and allocation system that converts high-touch customer signals (top accounts / escalations) into timeboxed cycle lanes with clear commitment SLAs and fallbacks. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc roadmap churn, give sales/CS predictable outcomes for escalations, and keep engineering capacity allocation aligned with OKRs.

Background: We currently accept top-account asks via a mix of Slack, support tickets and account engineering threads. That leads to opaque expectations, last-minute scope changes, and frequent interrupt-driven work that undermines sprint predictability. Existing intake artifacts (Drive: 'Account Intake Master v2', Confluence: 'VIP Escalation Playbook') capture qualitative signals but don't map to sprint/cycle capacity or automated fallbacks.

Objectives:
- Define a signal-to-lane mapping that translates account signals (ARR, renewal risk, product blocker, legal/regulatory need) into a small set of cycle lanes (Fastpass, Priority, Standard, Deferred) with quantitative capacity budgets per lane.
- Create an algorithmic allocator that proposes which requests fit in the current cycle given known capacity and ongoing work, exposing trade-offs and required scope reductions.
- Build a lightweight workflow (PM + ENG + Sales) to approve allocations, surface rejections with reasons, and publish a customer-facing expectation note.

Why different: Instead of a purely priority score we emphasize capacity-aware commitment windows and explicit fallbacks (e.g., canary ship partial API, pilot feature, or committed engineering runway in 2 cycles). This reduces disputes and increases predictability for enterprise buyers.
acceptance_criteria: Signal schema documented and implemented in carb ingestion source (ARR, risk, blocker, SLA tier, legal deadline)
Mapping table that assigns any incoming top-account signal to one of four lanes (Fastpass, Priority, Standard, Deferred) with clear numeric capacity weightings
A prototype allocation UI in Console (mock) showing current cycle capacity and a proposed allocation plan for top-account asks
Approval workflow defined: who can approve Fastpass / Priority allocations and what artifacts are required
Customer communication template for accepted/rejected allocations
Metrics dashboard tracking lane utilization, acceptance rate, and mean time from escalation to committed PR (or documented fallback)
success_metrics: Reduce unplanned scope imported into the cycle by top-account escalations from avg 18% to <8% of sprint capacity within 2 cycles
Increase on-time delivery for accepted top-account asks to 85% in first 3 cycles
CS satisfaction (post-allocation) survey >= 4.2/5 for transparency and expectations
Time-to-decision on escalations median <= 3 business days
proposed_solution: 1) Define signals and weights: lightweight JSON schema that scores each request by ARR, renewal imminence, security/regulatory deadline, product-blocker severity, and strategic alignment.
2) Lanes and capacity: map scores to lanes with pre-allocated capacity % per lane (e.g., Fastpass 10% of top-account capacity, Priority 40%, Standard 30%, Deferred 20%).

3) Allocation engine: small service (owned by PM infra) that takes current cycle committed capacity (from sprint/estimate snapshots) and simulates inclusion/removal of requests producing a ranked plan and list of scope reductions required to fit. Exposes an "explain" view for transparency.
4) Governance: define approvers for each lane (Fastpass requires CS Director + Eng TL sign-off), SLAs for decisions, and a public customer note template in CRM.
5) Fallbacks: pre-approved fallback artifacts (pilot flags, reduced-scope deliverables, 2-cycle backlog hold) that are routable automatically if capacity cannot be found this cycle.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (this ticket): Scope and prototype mapping + sample allocations for current Cycle 2026-W10; gather stakeholder feedback
Phase 1: Implement allocation engine prototype and mock UI in Console for live review with Sales/CS + Eng leadership (Cycle 2026-W11)
Phase 2: Pilot with 3 strategic accounts for two cycles; measure impact and tune weights (2026-W12 to 2026-W18)
Phase 3: Full rollout and docs + playbook; integrate with CRM notifications and SLA tracking (target release console-2026.04)
Post-release: Quarterly review of weights and lane capacity; incorporate learnings into OKR cycle planning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signals are noisy and could be gamed by sales; Mitigation: require evidence attachments (contracts, renewal dates) and a CS attestation step
Risk: Engineering capacity estimates are stale; Mitigation: snapshot capacity from sprint planning + buffer reserved for known emergencies
Risk: Perceived unfairness from customers; Mitigation: publish a transparent decision rationale and fallback commitments
Risk: Allocation engine complexity; Mitigation: start with deterministic heuristics and simple linear packing before moving to optimization
